This study's own home/classroom manipulation (medium held constant) lands squarely on the context-equivalence pole (null d=0.02-0.14 across three outcomes, robust to covariates). Direction: supports 'context does not matter' for physical location specifically, mediated theoretically (not empirically) by presence (FE, p.8-10).

(P/anticipatory-application) Structural analogue, not identical design: Makransky et al. vary WHERE the same desktop-VR simulation is completed (home vs. classroom, medium constant) and find equivalence; Part III's vle-01 varies WHETHER the 3D application is used at all (APP vs. VID strata) and finds the VID stratum shows threshold-foreclosure (F1), friction-driven flight (F4), and value-skepticism (F6). The two studies are not in direct contradiction because they vary different variables (location vs. modal completeness) — a distinction this cluster's own construction.

(P/anticipatory-application) This unit is the cluster's closest empirical analogue to Part III's lab=VR / deployment=2D-PC poles: both designs test whether removing a controlled, supervised setting degrades outcomes from a simulation-based learning artifact. Useful whenever Part III needs a citable prior finding on deployment-context equivalence to contrast against its own VID-stratum frictions.

(P/anticipatory-application) The authors' presence-as-mediator claim is theoretical, not measured — a caution directly relevant to Part III's own F7 (presence self-report) findings, which likewise cannot establish presence as a causal mediator of the APP/VID outcome gap without a dedicated instrument.

(P/anticipatory-application) The authors' own flagged limitation — 38.75% consent rate, possible self-selection toward motivated/mastery-oriented students — parallels a caution worth carrying into Part III's own survey-response-rate discussion (873 open responses; composition caveats noted in vle-01).
